## Overview

Storm Tracker applies a simplified implementation of **SCAFET** ([Scalable Feature Extraction and Tracking](https://github.com/nbarjun/SCAFET)) to daily wind forecasts, identifying and mapping severe storms globally without manual intervention.

### The Methodology: SCAFET

Unlike traditional detection pipelines that rely on dataset-dependent intensity thresholds, SCAFET analyzes the **underlying geometric structure** of atmospheric phenomena using a mathematical shape index.

| Feature Type | Detection Mechanism |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Cyclonic Storms** | Convex cap-shaped surface geometry & vorticity peaks |
| **Atmospheric Rivers** | Continuous high-moisture spatial corridors |
| **Jet Streams** | Linear, high-velocity atmospheric bounds |

For complete mathematical definitions, review the [Geoscientific Model Development publication](https://gmd.copernicus.org/articles/17/301/2024/) or my [Ph.D. dissertation](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391666823_Characteristics_of_Atmospheric_Rivers_of_Past_Present_and_Future).

---

## Operational Workflow

:::{.grid}

:::{.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
:::{.card .mb-3}
:::{.card-body}
**1. Ingestion & Computation**
Retrieves daily global wind vectors from the [ECMWF Data Store](https://data.ecmwf.int/forecasts/) and derives global atmospheric vorticity fields.
:::
:::
:::

:::{.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
:::{.card .mb-3}
:::{.card-body}
**2. Geometric Extraction**
Applies shape-index filters to isolate convex atmospheric structures characteristic of active storm centers.
:::
:::
:::

:::{.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
:::{.card .mb-3}
:::{.card-body}
**3. Filtering & Tracking**
Filters low-amplitude noise to extract, rank, and track high-intensity cyclone trajectories.
:::
:::
:::

:::{.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
:::{.card .mb-3}
:::{.card-body}
**4. Automated Publishing**
Renders updated geo-referenced JSON outputs directly to the web dashboard every 24 hours.
:::
:::
:::

:::
